Adult ensemble musical • In development

The logline

After years supporting his family in Las Vegas, a gifted 6'8" basketball hopeful follows his Knicks dream to New York—then jeopardizes seven artists’ trust by turning their private lives into his inspirational publicity. To earn a professional chance, he must learn that caring for people does not mean owning their stories—or giving up his own.

Isaiah “Zay” Reed grew up in Las Vegas with Denise, a single mother working as a cabaret server and struggling with alcohol addiction. Her boyfriends were always “Uncle.” Ray was the one who stayed in Zay’s life: after his marriage to Denise ended, he kept coaching, filming practices and helping Zay plan a basketball future.

After graduation, Zay’s absent biological father died just as college basketball seemed possible. Only afterward did Zay discover the grant applications his father had submitted for him. Grieving, with Denise and Ray divorced, he turned away from the college opportunity to work and support his family. The paperwork could not undo a childhood of absence.

Years of shifts, training and saving finally buy a trip to New York and a shot at a G League tryout. The Knicks remain the dream. Seven working artists become his neighbors and collaborators—and then Zay mistakes their trust for permission.

The question isn’t whether they’re talented.

What will they refuse
to trade for success?

EVERY FALL HAS A RHYTHM.

The O is the ball.

It belongs inside the word. The same cap height. Recognizable seams. A bounce that becomes a beat, then leaves room for someone else.

The world stays dark and tactile. Basketball orange is restrained. Each person keeps their own light, even when all eight share the frame.

The ball keeps a hand-driven dribble as the flight travels from Las Vegas to New York City. At 100%, it settles above a Madison Square Garden blueprint. A loading bar carries the rhythm underneath.
